title: Today's top defense-tech headlines
big: 53 new stories since the last brief. The busiest areas: drones & air autonomy and missiles, hypersonics & munitions.

stories.h: Navy Contracts Ursa Major to Develop Rocket Motors for Next-gen Missile Programs
stories.what: The U.S. Navy contracted Ursa Major to develop solid rocket motors for the sea service’s future Naval Modular Missile and Compact Air-to-Air Missile, the defense firm announced last week.
stories.you: The Navy is short of ships and is turning to cheaper unmanned boats, which opens the door to new builders.

stories.h: Leonardo DRS wins $500M slot to supply counter-drone radar
stories.what: Leonardo DRS has won a spot on a Pentagon counter-drone contract worth up to $500 million, giving the company a path to sell its tactical radars to Joint Interagency Task Force 401, the U.S.
stories.you: Drones are becoming the military's default purchase, so volume, price and reliability decide who wins.

stories.h: Lockheed gets $117M for Apache radar-hunting sensors
stories.what: The U.S. Army has awarded Lockheed Martin a $117.1 million contract to keep supporting the second-generation radar frequency interferometer on its Apache attack helicopters, a passive sensor that lets crews find and pinpoint enemy radars without giving away…
stories.you: Better sensors and navigation that works without GPS are prerequisites for everything autonomous.

stories.h: Avio, Lockheed sign agreement for solid rocket motor production
stories.what: The deal will pave a path for Avio USA to become a new provider of motors on Lockheed Martin’s Extended Range GMLRS and the Precision Strike Missile.
stories.you: More of the military's sensing and communications now runs through orbit, and new suppliers are getting in.

stories.h: Didn’t get picked for IFPC interceptor competition? Army says come demo anyway
stories.what: The service will continue working with the Lockheed Martin and Boeing-Anduril teams but also hosting “shoot-off opportunity” for additional vendors, explained Lt. Gen. Frank Lozano.
stories.you: Missile defense is one of the biggest budget lines this decade, and its software and sensors are open to newcomers.

watch.why: Around November 3. Whether US commercial growth keeps outpacing government revenue.

idea.h: Contract intelligence and capture agent for small vendors
idea.why: An LLM agent that watches SAM.gov, DIU, OTA consortia, budget documents and portfolio acquisition executives, matches openings to a product, and drafts responses. Thousands of new vendors are navigating DAWG and the new acquisition rules; turning valuations into orders is the stated test.
